story.mp3: The light at seven, I moved here last week. From my kitchen window, I see one window across the courtyard. At seven o'clock, the light comes on. A man wakes up, he makes coffee, he reads at the table. At half past 10, he turns off the light. He does the same thing every night. Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday. I know his week better than mine. On Friday, the light doesn't come on. Seven o'clock, quarter past seven, half past seven. The window stays dark. He doesn't wake up. He doesn't make coffee. I don't sleep well. On Saturday, the light comes on at eight. There are two cups on the table. They make coffee, they read. At 11, they turn off the light. On Sunday, he sees me at my window. He waves. I go down and we drink coffee, the three of us. His granddaughter arrived on Friday night. That is all it was.
